word_of_the_day.usage: Fresh milk was out of stock at the supermarket.

questions.question: In your daily routine (Market & Grocery Shopping), which sentence is grammatically natural?

options.a: I am usually out of stock every morning.
options.b: I usually out of stock every morning.
options.c: I usually out of stocks every morning.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Habitual daily actions take the Simple Present tense (I usually out of stock). Never pair 'am' directly with a base action verb.

questions.question: When describing an action you are doing at home right now, select the correct response:

options.a: I am tidying up the living room right now.
options.b: I tidying up the living room right now.
options.c: I am tidy up the living room right now.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Actions in progress require the Present Continuous form (am + verb-ing).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Out of stock' mean in daily conversation?

options.a: To run fast in a race.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'Out of stock' means: Temporarily unavailable in store. Example: "Fresh milk was out of stock at the supermarket."

questions.question: Which term best fits: 'Sorry I'm late, fresh vegetables were __________ at the market.'
questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'Out of stock' means goods or produce are temporarily unavailable in store.

questions.question: Listen to the audio clip. What is the speaker requesting you to do?

options.a: Stop what you are doing and leave immediately.
options.b: Pick up a fresh packet of tea from the store on your way home.
options.c: Call a taxi for tomorrow morning.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
The speaker asks: 'Could you please pick up a fresh packet of tea from the store on your way home?'
questions.audio_prompt: Could you please pick up a fresh packet of tea from the store on your way home?

questions.question: Listen to the second audio clip. What is the core message?

options.a: The speaker wants to drop by your place this evening for a quick chat.
options.b: The speaker is cancelling all plans for the week.
options.c: The speaker is asking for directions to the bus station.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
The speaker says: 'Hey! I'll drop by your place this evening around 6:00 PM for a quick chat.'
questions.audio_prompt: Hey! I will drop by your place this evening around 6:00 PM for a quick chat.

questions.question: How should you politely ask a neighbor or colleague for assistance?

options.b: Could you please lend me a hand with this for a minute?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'Lend a hand' is a courteous, friendly idiom for asking for assistance politely.

questions.question: Choose the most polite way to decline an invitation when you are busy:

options.a: I would love to come, but I have a prior commitment.
options.b: No, I am not coming to your house.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'I would love to come, but...' acknowledges the invitation warmly while declining politely.

questions.question:
Translate this Telugu daily scenario to natural conversational English:

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick and give some fresh ones.")

options.a: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick and give some fresh ones.
options.b: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out some fresh ones for me.
options.c: I morning wake up and tea drinking.

questions.explanation:
AI Feedback & Scoring (9/10):
Use 'per kilo' when asking price by weight, and 'pick out' or 'select' for choosing fresh produce.

Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out some fresh ones for me."
